rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~97% 25bp / ~3% 50bp (CME FedWatch via Hercules); ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~44%; RBA minutes 6–3
rows.read: Firm US retail sales pushed bets on a December Fed hike even higher, while the chance of a bigger half-point move all but disappeared. Europe, Britain and Japan are still expected to hike, Canada and New Zealand look more likely to wait, and Australia's board is split. US rates still look set to rise fastest, which keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US retail sales Oct +0.2% m/m (fcst +0.1%), control +0.6%; industrial production Oct −0.4% (fcst +0.1%), manufacturing +0.3%; NAHB builder index 25, lowest since April 2012; Japan Q3 GDP −0.1% annualized
rows.read: US shoppers kept spending in October, but US housing is clearly struggling and factory output was mixed. Japan's economy shrank in the summer and euro-area factories are barely growing. The US still looks firmer than most, which supports the dollar, though the gap is no longer widening.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: UK regular pay 3.5% 3m/y (fcst 3.5%; prior 3.7%); NZ two-year inflation expectations 2.36% (Q3 2.34%); UK CPI Oct fcst 3.6%, Wed Nov 18 1:00 AM CT
rows.read: UK pay growth cooled in line with forecasts, so UK inflation figures early Wednesday matter more for the pound. New Zealand businesses' inflation expectations barely moved, giving its central bank no new reason to hike. US inflation is still well above the Fed's goal, which keeps the pressure on to raise rates.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Dow ~−1.6%, S&P 500 ~−1%, Nasdaq ~−0.7% late Tuesday (AP); USD/JPY 159.35; AUD/USD 0.6736; NZD/USD 0.5494
rows.read: US stocks fell for a second day before Nvidia's results, with almost every sector lower. That helped the yen a little and weighed on the Aussie and kiwi, which track market mood. A confirmed US strike on an Iranian missile site added to the unease without setting off a wider scare.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$92.87 (+0.6%), WTI ~$84.39 (−1.2%); gold ~$3,847 (−0.5%); Global Dairy Trade index flat
rows.read: Oil swung between a supply glut and fresh Gulf attacks and ended little changed, so the Canadian dollar got no real help. Gold slid again toward a 13-month low, which adds to the Aussie's troubles. Flat dairy prices left the kiwi without a lift from its main export.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC report of Nov 10 (out late after Veterans Day): hedge funds for USD, GBP, AUD and gold; against EUR, NZD, CAD and CHF; slightly against JPY; real money disagrees on EUR, GBP and AUD
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.11% at the close
rows.read: Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs above 5%. They eased a little on Tuesday as investors sought safety in Treasuries. France's debt troubles keep weighing on the euro.
